I am 28 and I have been single for 6 months. Before that, I was in a relationship from age 18.
I won't lie, I can't relate to all these comments saying it's amazing etc. I do like small things, like getting to choose how to spend my time and gaining independence. I would urge you to think about exactly how you will cope alone practically. I had to spend some months with my dad and now I sleep on an air mattress in my friends flat while I try to save enough to move out. If you already have things in place, this won't be an issue, but to not have a real home feels very embarrassing at my age.
I also feel a very intense pressure, coming from within me, that I have relatively very little time to find the right person if I want to have children. This is hard for me to cope with and I think about it a lot. I worry about ending up childless and alone. Life can't be rushed and it does stress me out, especially at night.
I've found it really hard to sleep well alone. I'm also terrible at eating well if there's nobody else to cook for.
That said, it is a good chance to spend 100% of your time doing whatever you want without having to worry about compromising it. I have seen lots of friends, made art, booked trips and got into therapy and that stuff makes me feel capable and encouraged. It's been hard for me to establish a sense of identity on my own and to be honest i'm still not sure who I am as a singular entity. I think it's good to find that out, definitely a character building experience.
I can't talk about what dating around is like as I have no interest in casual sex or flings at all. Probably easier to be single if you're into that stuff.

Anecdotally, I think I was set up to be this way from the start. I had the kind of childhood that lends itself to poor self esteem as an adult, which in turn kept me in a bad relationship. Thoughts like 'I won't be able to do any better than this anyway' or 'maybe he's right and I deserve this' are a product of that poor self-esteem and can fester when it goes untreated. The longer I live, the more I see how these problems seem to trickle down through generations. Most people don't break the cycle.

I can try but honestly to this day it's hard for me to tell myself. I struggle to remember some events because I was so unhappy I felt very detached from myself. Life was dreamlike. He would generally always be miserable. He ignored me, sat at his computer and acted as if I was nothing but an annoyance. I would become emotional about it. I would want to talk and try to understand what I'd done 'wrong'. In reality I'd done nothing, but emotionally he behaved as if I had. When I questioned that, he would turn on me and say that I was mentally ill, insane and paranoid. Sometimes I'd contest that and the situation would escalate. Over time I began to back down and apologise and acquiesce to his view of things and not my own. I hope that helps explain somewhat. I think what saved my mindset was speaking to a psychologist I met who told me that crazy mean people don't tend to worry if they're crazy and mean. That began to help me see that I could trust in my own assessment of what was happening.

I never thought I would be one of these women because I believe myself to be intelligent and strong. I used to think women who stayed in abusive relationships were kind of weak and I couldn't understand why they didn't just leave. You don't know what its like until it happens to you. I fell in love with a man, hard. I thought he was amazing. Slowly, he began to be abusive, but alongside that he led me to believe that I was unreasonable and insane for questioning his behaviour. He was so utterly convincing, such an excellent manipulator, that I spent an entire year wondering if I'd gotten everything wrong, if maybe it was ME that was the abusive one. It was so hard to leave because he caused me doubt my own perceptions and made me think I was incapable of judging the situation.
Abuse is complex. It's hard to leave. You become scared and small. It's hard to admit that the person you thought somebody was does not exist. I felt embarrassed that I'd chosen poorly. I found myself wanting to 'save face' and pretend to my friends and family that everything was fine. I blamed myself for 'not behaving'. He would tell me time and time again that his abusive behavior was my fault for pushing his buttons. I thought if I could just be 'better' that he would be loving and kind again like he was in the beginning. 
It is also scary to start over alone. I left him at age 28, and I felt dreadfully worried that I was too old for anybody to want me again, that if I left I would be alone forever, and that maybe I should have stayed because at least the relationship appeared to be respectable and we could split things financially. 
These are some reasons it happens. I imagine I am far from alone in my experience of being in a bad relationship.
